key_insight: This study maps demographic-associated information in routine tissue images at health-system scale, covering 1.3 million slides across 25 organs. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so the strength and consistency of demographic prediction cannot be determined.
problem_solved: It remains unclear how broadly tissue images contain information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race across organs and disease states.
method: Analyze 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs.
Use pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to assess demographic-associated information.
Systematically evaluate 69 organ–demographic combinations involving sex, age group, and self-reported race.
impact: The study addresses a potential source of confounding in pathology AI: image representations may carry demographic-associated information alongside disease signals. Mapping this information can guide subgroup evaluation and robustness checks, but does not by itself establish bias or causality.
visual_elements: Scale panel highlighting 1.3 million slides, 257,322 patients, and 25 organs.
Workflow diagram: tissue slide → foundation-model representation → multiple-instance learning → demographic assessment.
Organ-by-demographic matrix showing the 69 evaluated combinations, without unsupported performance values.
Evaluation checklist linking demographic information to confounding, subgroup performance, and robustness.
paper_title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
paper_authors: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare, Paula Restrepo, Jannes Jegminat
